score.details.recovery.label: Body Recovery
score.details.recovery.description:
Physical recovery is a very important aspect to take into consideration when checking your overall condition. Especially after high or medium intensity activities, your body and heart need time to repair. When over exercising, there is up to a 72 hours window of impaired immunity. This basically means virus and bacteria may have an easier time infecting your body.

Kira automatically checks your activity volume in the past 48 hours. Medium and high intensity activities combined should not exceed a total of 240 cardio points.


Even though you might be able to do more, the scientific literature is clear on the subject, it is unhealthy to exceed such amounts without recovery and without tiring your muscles and heart.
score.details.wake_up.label: Wake up score
score.details.wake_up.description:
The wake up score measures your level of sleep inertia when you wake up based on the stage you woke up in and what part of that stage you were in.


While it is a great measure to take into consideration for your energy levels, it mostly affects the beginning of your day even though inertia might affect your attention in the afternoon. This is why it has a lighter weight in the calculation of your energy.
score.details.breathing.label: Breathing rate
score.details.breathing.description:
Breathing rate reported in respirations (breaths) per minute is an indicator of your cardiovascular load and is a good indicator of your wellbeing. You breathe harder and faster when you are ill or in need of energy. 


This metric varies much less than your RHR and HRV and is therefore much more stable. It becomes very useful when it increases a lot compared to your Reference. This metric acts as a threshold that can warn you when something is highly unusual. The difference between your daily value and your Reference shows to what degree you are in good condition or not. Normal values for a resting adult ranges from 12 to 18 breaths per minute.
score.details.hrv.label: Heart rate variability
score.details.hrv.description:
HRV measures the specific changes in time between successive heartbeats and is a great measure of your autonomic nervous system. It is used to see how well you recover after certain events. It is also a good measure of stress and anxiety and can unveil many things about your overall wellbeing.


HRV is highly personal and variations are measured against your own Reference. Anything above means that your body and immune system are ready to tackle challenges during an upcoming day whereas the contrary would probably mean that you need to focus on recovering, basically resuming a healthy pace of life and sleep well. The difference between your daily value and your Reference shows to what degree you are in good condition or not.
score.details.resting_heart_rate.label: Resting heart rate
score.details.resting_heart_rate.descrip:
RHR is a great measure for your overall health, readiness and fitness. A low resting heart rate is an indication of a strong heart muscle that can pump out a greater amount of blood with every beat so it does not have to beat as frequently. Generally speaking, the lower it is, the better.


A higher RHR compared to your Reference indicates poor overall wellness conditions, that you shoud avoid too much mental and physical stress and concentrate on recovering. If your daily RHR is lower than your Reference then your body is ready for intense stress. 


Kira also compares your Reference with the References of people of the same physiology to assess where you stand in terms of fitness. The difference between your daily value and your Reference shows to what degree you are in good condition or not.
score.details.temperature.label: Temperature variation
score.details.temperature.description:
This contributor looks at the temperature variations occurring throughout your sleep compared to your baseline. It an essential metric to evaluate how your natural defenses respond to your environement. 

When the variation is higher than +/- 0.8 degrees Celcius, that’s when you need to start paying attention. An advice would be measuring your body temperature with a thermometer. 

Any variance above or under your baseline can give a lot of crucial information. It can fluctuate with activity, your nutrition, your circadian rhythm, can indicate that your body fights against an illness, can reflect external environment changes such as a season change and can even reflect a woman’s menstrual cycle very clearly. 

Typically, the pattern for menstrual cycles is a temperature drop from your periods through your ovulation phase, followed by a rise from the end of your ovulation until the beginning of your next periods.
score.details.sleep_quality.label: Sleep quality
score.details.sleep_quality.description:
The Sleep Quality contributor is based on a longer term view of your sleep quality patterns. Having slept very poorly two nights ago, even by having slept well yesterday night will have a negative impact on your energy today.


Kira looks at the past two days of your sleep quality. The sleep quality score takes a number of contributors into consideration to determine whether it was poor, good or optimal.


The main takeaway is to consider that a score below 80 would mean that your overall sleep quality was poor, which will negatively affect the energy levels. On the contrary, anything over 80 is quite good and is a great indicator of how good you will feel throughout the day both physically and mentally.
score.details.sleep_balance.label: Sleep balance
score.details.sleep_balance.description:
The Sleep Balance contributor is based on a long term view of your sleep duration patterns. 


Kira compares the past two days of your sleep duration to your long-term sleep history as well as to the ideal amount of sleep duration for people of your chronotype and age. It's advised that for staying healthy and alert, adults typically need 7-9 hours of sleep every night.
score.details.activity_volume.label: Activity volume
score.details.activity_volume.descriptio:
Activity Volume measures the amount of cardio points you've gotten over the past 7 days. It is an essential aspect of maintaining and improving your fitness level. 


Kira bases her calculations on two key components. One is making sure you are respecting the medical recommendations (at least 150 cardio points per week) and the other is making sure that you have an activity load that is suitable to your activity habits.

banner.calibration.message: Keep wearing your ring during the entirety of the {days} days calibration period for improved results!
calibration.recommandation.1:
Hi, {username}, this is Kira. I would like to welcome you to the Circular tribe! 👋

Your Circular app will allow you to check your recommendations and detailed biometrics, set up an alarm clock, edit your alerts, and so much more!
calibration.recommandation.2:
Through Circular, checking and improving your health & sleep while optimizing your activities becomes easy 💪

On top of that, you'll be able to know more about yourself and understand the effects of your environment on your wellbeing. Nothing complicated, everything will be made easy to understand! That's my job!
calibration.recommandation.3: In order to get the most of your Circular, I strongly suggest that you wear the ring as much as possible (night & day) and that you answer the questions I might be asking on your feed. They help me refine each recommendation to your needs and profile.
calibration.recommandation.4:
Hi, me again.

As I need to get to know you better, we're going to dive into a 14-day calibration period. During that time, I may need to ask you some questions to better understand you and refine my reasoning. During this calibration period, features will be limited. What's in it for you after that period? Every recommendation will be ultra-personalized and you will learn about yourself like never before! Let's do this 🔥
calibration.recommandation.5:
So what am I doing exactly during these 14 days, you may ask?

I'm currently setting up what I call your "References". You have one for each important biometric. A Reference is a value for a given metric that refers to your normal state. You will be able to use References to compare your daily metrics against it to know if you are doing well or not. References are displayed under graphs, inside of the Sleep and Activity circles.

In addition to setting up your References, I will analyze your habits altogether, whether it is your sleep or your activity. I'll define a personalized profile, define your chronotype, and much more!

During this 14 day period, you can go ahead and live your usual lifestyle, I'll take care of the rest 😎
calibration.recommandation.6: My first question will allow me to adjust the default vibration intensity of your alarm clock to your needs ⏰
calibration.recommandation.6.question.la: Do you think you can effectively stand guard while you sleep?
calibration.recommandation.6.question.op: Yes, because I know I wake up easily when something unexpected happens.
No, because once I sleep, I can't hear anything.
calibration.recommandation.7: I've adjusted the default vibration intensity to your needs, but you can always change it, in the alarm clock settings by clicking on "edit vibration".

sleep.details.title: Sleep details
sleep.duration.title: Sleep duration
sleep.quality.disturbance.label: Disturbances
sleep.quality.disturbance.description:
Calculated in minutes, they correspond to the times you were awake during your sleep. 


The minutes are added up and help to calculate real sleep. Waking up several times during your sleep is natural but too much time awake might reflect sleeping disorders or overall poor sleep quality. 


The displayed percentage corresponds to how much you have been awake from the moment you fell asleep up to the moment you woke up. More than 20% of the time is considered unhealthy and might be caused by many internal or external factors.
sleep.quality.real_sleep.label: Real sleep
sleep.quality.real_sleep.description:
Real sleep is a derivative of sleep efficiency. While total sleep includes the entire sleep period and does not take into account disturbances, real sleep takes into account the disturbances and reflects the time you actually slept during your sleep period.


It is a great indicator of overall sleep quality as a sleep efficiency percentage that is too high reflects many disturbances (internal or external factors keeping you awake).  


Anything below 80% is considered poor and will negatively impact your sleep quality score. Reciprocally, a real sleep score over 90% is optimal. Anything in between is good!
sleep.quality.tranquility.label: Tranquility
sleep.quality.tranquility.description: It determines how much you have moved in total volume and evaluates the number of position changes during your sleep. An agitated night is often a sign of reduced sleep quality. We divide the score you see in 3 indicators: agitated, still and peaceful.
sleep.quality.circadian.label: Circadian rhythm
sleep.quality.circadian.description:
Circadian rhythm is a process that regulates a lot of your biological events. It is basically a 24-hour internal clock that is running in the background of your brain that sends powerful physiological signals to promote wakefulness and sleep at specific times of the day. Your chronotype which is genetic has a lot of influence on the schedules.


In order for this process to be optimal, there are several factors that need to be taken into account, the two main ones being the constency of your sleep schedule and the alignment of your sleep with the circadian rhythm of your time zone.


Kira will automatically compare your usual sleep schedule to your weekly history to determine whether you are following a consistent rhythm and will also analyze the midpoint of your sleep to see if it is aligned with the light–dark cycles and with your own chronotype.
sleep.quality.rem.label: REM sleep
sleep.quality.rem.description:
REM sleep is the stage which is responsible for restoration and memory consolidation. REM sleep is also known by the fact that dreams appear during this stage.


The displayed percentage is your total REM sleep time divided by your night's total sleep. 

The recommended value depends on many factors including age, you should target between 20-25% of your Real sleep. 


Kira knows your needs and will take into consideration if you had enough REM or if you are deprived of it to measure overall sleep quality.
sleep.quality.deep.label: Deep sleep
sleep.quality.deep.description:
Deep Sleep is the stage that allows the reparation of muscles and tissues, that stimulates growth, boosts immune function, and builds up energy for the next day. The displayed percentage is your total deep sleep time divided by your total sleep. 


The recommended value depends on a lot of factors. As a rule of thumb you should approximately target 15-20% deep sleep.


Kira knows your needs and will take into consideration if you have had enough deep sleep or if you are deprived of it to measure overall sleep quality.
sleep.quality.fall_asleep.label: Time to fall asleep
sleep.quality.fall_asleep.description:
Also known as sleep latency, it is the length of time that it takes to accomplish the transition from full wakefulness to sleep.
 

Your time to fall asleep can be modified by internal or external factors such as caffeine, device screens, heat and many other factors.


Kira compares your night's latency to your baseline latency and compares it to scientific norms to give a score. Sleep specialists agree to say that a sleep latency below 5 minutes is not normal and anything above 30 minutes is too much.
sleep.quality.debt.label: Sleep debt
sleep.quality.debt.description:
Sleep debt is the cumulative effect of not getting enough sleep or getting too much sleep. 


A negative sleep debt means that you slept less than you needed and a positive sleep debt means that you overslept.

While negative sleep debt is bad for your body, positive sleep debt is inefficient and unproductive. 


Sleep debt looks at how much you have actually slept (Real sleep) compared to your personal sleeping length needs. Any deviation from your personal needs whether more or less sleep will impact negatively your sleep debt indicator.
